model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of a language model, including a baseline "Vanilla" model and various configurations of SepLLM and StrmLLM. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration: a light purple line for "Vanilla", a blue line for "StrmLLM (n=64)", an orange line for "SepLLM (n=64)", a green line for "SepLLM (n=64, H)", a red line for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", and a dark blue line for "SepLLM (n=128)". All lines start at approximately 3.4 loss at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the initial phase, followed by a gradual convergence. The "Vanilla" model (light purple) reaches a final loss of about 2.5 at 140,000 iterations. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" (blue) consistently shows the highest loss throughout training, ending at approximately 2.6. The "SepLLM (n=64)" (orange) and "SepLLM (n=64, H)" (green) show similar performance, with losses converging to around 2.52 and 2.51, respectively. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" (red) and "SepLLM (n=128)" (dark blue) achieve the lowest losses, both stabilizing near 2.5 by the end of training. Each line has slight noise or variance, indicated by small fluctuations, particularly in the early iterations.
